title: Laredo Book Festival Returns Dec. 5 With Bestselling Minecraft Author Mark Cheverton
excerpt: The free Laredo Book Festival returns Saturday, Dec. 5, to the Joe A. Guerra Laredo Public Library, with bestselling author Mark Cheverton headlining a lineup of 13 authors and illustrators.
content:
The Laredo Book Festival is coming back to the Joe A. Guerra Laredo Public Library on Saturday, Dec. 5, 2026, from 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m., with a free day of authors, illustrators, stories and children's activities for all ages.

The festival, billed as a celebration of stories and community, is headlined by bestselling author Mark Cheverton, according to the Laredo Public Library. Cheverton, a former physics teacher and research scientist, is the author of the Gameknight999 series of Minecraft-inspired novels. His books have sold more than 2 million copies worldwide, have been published in 31 countries and translated into 27 languages.

Cheverton's latest novel, Facing the Beast Within, follows a sixth grader who must stop a demon lord from invading Earth while finding his way through his own anxiety, according to the library.

Twelve more authors and illustrators round out the lineup: Annette Gonzalez-Avila, Gabriela Mendoza-Garcia, Ricardo Guerrero, Claudia and Christopher Diaz, Rosario Ozuna, Suzette Bishop, Kevin Riha, Cynthia Dougherty-Bernal, Juan Ramirez, Sandra Cavazos Ayala, Patty York Raymond and Roy Gonzales. The Diaz duo's bilingual children's book, Alejandro and the Bacon Breakfast, was once read aloud by astronaut Nick Hague from space, according to the library.

The festival will also feature children's activities, appearances by book characters and local vendors. H-E-B and Ballet Folklorico are among the sponsors and partners.

The library is also warning authors about a phishing attempt: a fake email circulating in the literary community asks authors to pay a registration fee for the festival. The library says it does not charge authors any registration or participation fee, and anyone unsure about a message should call the library directly at 956-795-2400 to verify it.
